open_points.subject: A11 attempt numbering for skipped/upstream nodes
open_points.text: "attempt_number numbers the attempts... each execution of a function element, and each start of a send of an operation element, takes the next number; nothing else takes one" and later "A node recorded `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed` was never attempted; its one record carries attempt number 1."
open_points.question: Are `skipped_by_guard`/`upstream_failed` records outside the attempt sequence (with a fixed sentinel `attempt_number=1`), or do they participate in the same per-element attempt counter rules?
options: Use `attempt_number=1` as a sentinel for non-attempt records
Advance the normal per-element counter even for non-executed records
Store no attempt number for non-attempt records
open_points.default_guess: Use sentinel `attempt_number=1` for non-attempt records and do not advance execution/send counters.

open_points.subject: A16 pagination size over max
open_points.text: "Every list operation returns at most `page_size_default` items unless the caller asks for fewer or more, never more than `page_size_max`"
open_points.question: If a caller requests a page size greater than `page_size_max`, does the kernel clamp to `page_size_max` or refuse the request?
options: Clamp to `page_size_max`
Refuse as schema/validation error

open_points.subject: A16 pagination continuation behavior
open_points.text: "...newest first — in reverse store order (K-17) — with a continuation token"
open_points.question: What exact continuation-token semantics are required (stable snapshot vs live cursor), and are duplicates/skips across concurrent new records allowed?
options: Snapshot semantics: no duplicates/skips across pages
Live cursor semantics over store order; duplicates/skips may occur with concurrent writes
Opaque token behavior left implementation-defined
open_points.default_guess: Live cursor over store order with possible movement under concurrent writes.

open_points.subject: A04 'try implementation' named-case handling
open_points.text: "...executes an existing implementation on the cases of its contract version's corpus that the request names, all of them when it names none, in corpus order"
open_points.question: How must the kernel handle named case lists that include unknown case ids, duplicate ids, or ids outside the implementation's contract version corpus?
options: Refuse the whole request on any invalid/foreign/duplicate case id
Ignore invalid ids and run only valid unique corpus cases
Run duplicates as repeated executions
open_points.default_guess: Refuse on any unknown/foreign case id; de-duplicate duplicates before execution.

open_points.subject: A03 missing sandbox dependency behavior for execution-producing actions
open_points.text: "without both [bubblewrap present and probe succeeds] it serves no execution and says why" and "refuses every execution naming the missing sandbox"
open_points.question: For actions that imply multiple executions or side effects (submit implementation/admission, run flow with function nodes, startup recovery), is the whole action refused before creating/changing records, or does it proceed and record execution failures?
options: Refuse the action pre-execution with no new run/admission artifacts
Proceed and record per-execution failures (e.g., sandbox_violation/crashed)
Mixed behavior per action
open_points.default_guess: Refuse pre-execution for actions requiring sandbox execution.

open_points.subject: A14 startup recovery vs A03 no-execution mode
open_points.text: A14: "On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel ... advances ... every run left `running`: a function element ... is executed again" versus A03: "without both [sandbox checks] it serves no execution"
open_points.question: If the kernel restarts with unresolved `running` runs but sandbox execution is unavailable, must startup recovery block startup, skip recovery, or mark affected runs to a terminal/waiting state?
options: Block startup until sandbox execution is available
Start without recovery and leave runs unchanged
Start and transition affected runs to a defined non-running state
open_points.default_guess: Start without recovery and leave affected runs unchanged until execution becomes available.

open_points.subject: A09 request construction when path placeholders exist
open_points.text: "every `{name}` in the path takes the input port of that name... for `GET` and `DELETE` the other `value` inputs are query parameters... for other methods they form one JSON object body keyed by port name"
open_points.question: For non-GET/DELETE methods, does the JSON body include path-bound input ports as well, or only non-path inputs?
options: Include all value inputs, including those used in path placeholders
Include only non-path value inputs
open_points.default_guess: Include only non-path value inputs in JSON body.

open_points.subject: A09 outcome mapping for malformed/non-final HTTP responses
open_points.text: Outcome table covers "no status received", 2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx, but does not state handling for malformed status lines/protocol errors after send or informational-only/invalid final status handling.
open_points.question: How should malformed HTTP responses or protocol violations after request bytes are sent be classified (`service_unreachable`, `operation_failed`, or `outcome_unknown`)?
options: Treat as "may have been sent, no status received"
Treat as contract/protocol failure (`operation_failed`)
Different mapping for read vs non-read
open_points.default_guess: Classify as "no valid status received": `service_unreachable` for read, `outcome_unknown` for non-read.
